newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND TURN TO HOLLIOAKES TO SAVE FACE AND SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND TURN TO HOLLIOAKES TO SAVE FACE AND SERIES.

text.p: England are counting on a breath of antipodean air to provide them with an essential shot in the arm in the fifth test against Australia starting on Thursday.

The Hollioake brothers, both from Melbourne but both strongly and devotedly English, have been called in to rescue the struggling home side who must win the final two tests to prevent Australia retaining the Ashes.

As English cricket considers proposals put forward this week to improve its long-term prospects, the national team are hoping the Hollioake boys can supply the missing ingredient to help England meet their short-term target.
Failure to win at Trent Bridge will mean that Australia, two-one up with two matches to play, retain the Ashes, as they have done since 1989.
A victory would leave the series hanging in the balance for the final test at The Oval later this month.

It may smack of a desperation measure, but the two brothers both seem certain to start. Adam, the Surrey captain, and 19-year-old Ben starred in the one-day international series earlier in the season, when England achieved what has since turned out to have been a misleading 3-0 whitewash.

The psychological high of that success carried them though to a first test triumph at Edgbaston, even without the Hollioakes, who have been summoned after demoralising drubbings in the third and fourth matches of the six-test series.
England were beaten by 268 runs at Old Trafford and by an innings and 61 runs at Headingley, only once passing 200 runs in any of their four innings.
Doubts exist about the true test-match quality of the brothers, but the same doubts apply to the men they have replaced, opener Mark Butcher and all-rounder Mark Ealham.
What the newcomers do have is the undimmed enthusiasm of youngsters yet to suffer the sort of defeats handed out to their seniors over the past six weeks.
Ben Hollioake's vibrant 98 in the recent Benson and Hedges Cup final at Lord's to follow his 63 there in the one-day international confirmed that he does not lack big-match temperament either.
Paceman Andy Caddick, born and bred in New Zealand, will return to the side after being dropped for Mike Smith and there may have to be another change in the attack.
Darren Gough, who has taken 16 wickets in the series, says he is struggling to overcome a knee injury, and Devon Malcolm has been placed on stand-by.
With heavy rain forecast for much of the country, England, as usual, will keep their options open until the morning of the match on a pitch traditionally favourable to batsmen.
Australia, having strengthened a formidable team even further by bringing in gifted young stroke-player Ricky Ponting for Michael Bevan in the last test, see no reason to make any further changes.

Teams: England (from)- Michael Atherton (captain), Alec Stewart, John Crawley, Nasser Hussain, Graham Thorpe, Adam Hollioake, Ben Hollioake, Robert Croft, Darren Gough, Andy Caddick, Dean Headley, Devon Malcolm, Phil Tufnell.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Elliott, Greg Blewett, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Ricky Ponting, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath.
